SETUP GUIDE

## Connect Slack MCP Tool with your Agent

TypeScriptPython

1

#### Install Composio

typescript

Copy

```typescript
npm install @composio/core ai @ai-sdk/mcp @ai-sdk/openai
```

Install the Composio SDK and your agent framework

2

#### Create a session with MCP enabled

typescript

Copy

```typescript
import { Composio } from "@composio/core";

const composio = new Composio();
const { mcp } = await composio.create("your-user-id", {
  toolkits: ["slack"],
  mcp: true,
});
```

Create a session scoped to Slack and read its MCP URL and headers

3

#### Connect your agent to the MCP server

typescript

Copy

```typescript
import { createMCPClient } from "@ai-sdk/mcp";
import { openai } from "@ai-sdk/openai";
import { generateText, stepCountIs } from "ai";

const client = await createMCPClient({
  transport: { type: "http", url: mcp.url, headers: mcp.headers },
});

const { text } = await generateText({
  model: openai("gpt-5.6-sol"),
  tools: await client.tools(),
  prompt: "Send reminder to sales channel tomorrow",
  stopWhen: stepCountIs(10),
});

console.log(text);
await client.close();
```

Pass the session's MCP URL and headers to your agent and run a Slack request

SETUP GUIDE

## Connect Slack API Tool with your Agent

TypeScriptPython

1

#### Install Composio

typescript

Copy

```typescript
npm install @composio/core @composio/openai openai
```

Install the Composio SDK, the OpenAI provider, and the OpenAI SDK

2

#### Create a Composio session

typescript

Copy

```typescript
import OpenAI from "openai";
import { Composio } from "@composio/core";
import { OpenAIResponsesProvider } from "@composio/openai";

const composio = new Composio({ provider: new OpenAIResponsesProvider() });
const client = new OpenAI();

const session = await composio.create("your-user-id", { toolkits: ["slack"] });
const tools = await session.tools();
```

Initialize Composio with the OpenAI Responses provider and create a session scoped to Slack

3

#### Run Slack tools with your agent

typescript

Copy

```typescript
let response = await client.responses.create({
  model: "gpt-5.6-sol",
  tools,
  input: [{ role: "user", content: "Send reminder to sales channel tomorrow" }],
});

while (response.output.some((o) => o.type === "function_call")) {
  const outputs = await composio.provider.handleToolCalls(session, response.output);
  response = await client.responses.create({
    model: "gpt-5.6-sol",
    tools,
    previous_response_id: response.id,
    input: outputs,
  });
}

console.log(response.output_text);
```

Send a request, execute the Slack tool calls through the session, and print the final answer

## Why Use Composio?

### AI Native Slack Integration

- Supports both Slack MCP and direct API based integrations
- Structured, LLM-friendly schemas for reliable tool execution
- Rich coverage for reading, writing, and querying your Slack data

### Managed Auth

- Built-in OAuth handling with automatic token refresh and rotation
- Central place to manage, scope, and revoke Slack access
- Per user and per environment credentials instead of hard-coded keys

### Agent Optimized Design

- Tools are tuned using real error and success rates to improve reliability over time
- Comprehensive execution logs so you always know what ran, when, and on whose behalf

### Enterprise Grade Security

- Fine-grained RBAC so you control which agents and users can access Slack
- Scoped, least privilege access to Slack resources
- Full audit trail of agent actions to support review and compliance

FAQ

## Frequently asked questions

### Do I need my own Slack developer credentials or OAuth app?+

No. Composio provides a managed OAuth app for Slack, so you sign in with your normal Slack account and approve access. If you later want the consent screen to show your own company name, you can add your own Slack OAuth app in the Composio dashboard, and every connection after that uses it.

### Can I use multiple toolkits together?+

Yes! Composio's Tool Router enables agents to use multiple toolkits. [Learn more](https://docs.composio.dev/tool-router/overview).

### Is Composio secure with my Slack account?+

Yes. Composio is SOC 2 Type II compliant and is built to keep your Slack connection and credentials secure. OAuth tokens and API keys are encrypted, and sensitive customer data is protected at rest and in transit.

Composio also undergoes independent security testing and continuously monitors its systems for security threats. You can review the latest reports and policies in the [Composio Trust Center](https://trust.composio.dev/).

### What if the API changes?+

Composio maintains and updates all toolkit integrations automatically, so your agents always work with the latest API versions.

### What can an agent do in Slack beyond messaging?+

Over 150 actions, like managing channels, reacting to messages, handling files, setting reminders and more.

### Can an agent respond to Slack activity automatically?+

Yes — new channels, new messages, direct messages, and reactions can all trigger it.

### Where are my Slack login details stored? +

In an encrypted vault, scoped to exactly the permissions you granted when connecting.

### What happens if a permission is missing?+

Slack blocks the action and shows an error. An admin needs to add that permission in Slack's settings — Composio won't quietly work around it.

### Does this work differently for large companies on Slack Enterprise Grid?+

Sometimes — a few actions need an exact channel ID instead of a channel name.

### How do I log in to Slack?+

A normal Slack login. You pick the workspace and approve the permissions once.

### Is my Slack data safe with Composio?+

Yes — SOC 2 Type II and ISO/IEC 27001:2022 certified, documented at trust.composio.dev.

### What's a real example of something an agent can do?+

"Send a reminder to the marketing channel at 10am" or "star this message from my manager."

### Does the agent act as me inside Slack?+

When you connect a Slack account through Composio, every action runs under that account, so anything the agent creates, sends, or changes shows up in Slack as done by you. Keep an approval step in your prompt for actions with side effects, such as sending or deleting, and have the agent draft first.

### Which Slack permissions does Composio get?+

Exactly the ones Slack lists on its consent screen when you connect. Review that screen before approving. If you connect a work account, your Slack administrator may need to approve the app first, and you can revoke the access inside Slack whenever you want.

### Can I use multiple Slack accounts with Claude and ChatGPT?+

Yes. Composio supports multiple connected accounts for the same app, and that works in Claude, ChatGPT, or any other assistant you connect through Composio. Give each Slack connection a name such as work or personal, and the assistant uses the one you mention in the request. Each account keeps its own credentials and nothing is merged.

### What happens when my Slack access expires or I revoke it?+

Composio refreshes Slack tokens automatically, so day to day you do nothing. If you revoke access inside Slack, or Slack invalidates the session, the connection shows as expired in Composio and the agent stops acting on that account until you reconnect it, which is a single sign-in.

### Does using Slack through Composio cost extra?+

Composio's free Hobby plan includes 100,000 tool calls per month with no credit card, and up to 20,000 of those can run through Composio-managed apps like Slack. Personal Slack use rarely gets near that. Paid plans add higher limits and team features, and Slack's own pricing is unaffected.

### How is Composio different from the Slack connectors already built into Claude and ChatGPT?+

Built-in connectors usually give one AI access to a limited set of apps. Many people use Composio because it lets their AI connect to more apps than it normally supports, or connect to multiple accounts for the same app (e.g. connect Claude to multiple Slack accounts).

With Composio, you connect Slack once and then use it across different AI assistants without setting it up separately in each one. Connect your apps to Composio once, then connect Composio to whichever AI you use, whether that's Claude, ChatGPT, Hermes, or your own custom assistant.
